assessment: As of the 2025-03-12T12:15:00Z cutoff, the scoped manufacturing records show one significant abnormality requiring immediate investigation: in-process batch BATCH-099 (Famotidine Injection, USP, sterile solution for injection, LINE-A, started 06:55Z) has two concurrent action-level microbiological control signals - environmental monitoring sample EM-0100 (process support area, gram-negative morphology) at 1.09 vs action limit 1.0 (status 'action', 11:05Z) and upstream bioburden result LAB-0300 at 1.71 vs action limit 1.0 (status 'action', 171% of the limit, sampled 10:55Z, reported exactly at the 12:15Z cutoff, corroborated in four sources: lims_export, microbiology_results, lims_review_local and the scanned lab review). This is the highest bioburden action-level result in the package: thirty-nine percent above BATCH-075's action-level result (2024-12-01) and roughly fifteen and a half percent above BATCH-084's (2025-01-04), both of which were followed the same day by HIGH-severity microbiology deviations (DEV-0003, DEV-0005) that remain OPEN with no recorded root cause. No deviation record exists for BATCH-099 as of the cutoff. Secondary findings requiring QA review: first, BATCH-075 and BATCH-084 were released and shipped (2024-12-16/2025-01-19 dispositions; 2025-01-02/2025-02-04 shipments) while their HIGH-severity microbiology deviations remained open, with no deviation-impact documentation in scope; second, PUMP-02 - used by BATCH-099 on 2025-03-12 - has two prior high-severity equipment_pressure_ratio excursions (SYN-0015 2024-04-05, SYN-0090 2025-01-30, the latter under open equipment deviation DEV-0007 with root cause not confirmed) and BATCH-099's own PROC-0398 reading (1.0552) sits near the 1.1 upper expected bound; third, an open recurring HIGH procedure deviation DEV-0008 (SYN-0091, recurrence_flag 1, root cause not confirmed). All deterministic screening flags and all priority candidates were confirmed as clock/data-quality limitations (missing process-clock basis), not process excursions. Key gaps: root causes of DEV-0003/DEV-0005/DEV-0007/DEV-0008 are unconfirmed; no SOP, QA release justification, retest or environmental-control records are in scope; historian and PDF coverage for BATCH-099 ends at 11:25Z (log endpoint, not proof of normal conditions); scanned-PDF citations are unverified OCR pending human visual review. Severity is proposed as HIGH (advisory): action-level microbiological excursions on a sterile product batch, a same-day escalation gap relative to site precedent, and release-with-open-deviation patterns. Final severity is determined by the configured routing policy. No disposition, release, CAPA or regulatory action is approved or executed by this investigation.
cross_scope_synthesis: Shared pattern across sources: the laboratory sources (lims_export, microbiology_results, lims_review_local, scanned_lab_review) independently corroborate the same action-level bioburden results for BATCH-075 (1.23), BATCH-084 (1.48) and BATCH-099 (1.71), each preceded the same morning by alert-level signals (PRE-LAB-001 0.79 / PRE-LAB-002 0.82 for the prior batches; EM-0100 1.09 and the alert-level pattern for BATCH-099), and each prior action-level result was followed within ~1.6-2.6 hours by a HIGH-severity microbiology deviation (DEV-0003 12:18Z, DEV-0005 12:43Z). BATCH-099 fits the laboratory and environmental pattern but breaks the quality-record pattern: no deviation exists for it as of the cutoff, while its batch record is still in process (no status/disposition cells). Exceptions: SYN-0004's historical action-level result (1.08, 2024-02-21) also has no deviation record, and SYN-0014's repeat result (1.06) is status 'invalidated', showing the lab pipeline can invalidate repeat samples; no such repeat/invalidation exists for BATCH-075/084/099. Equipment records do not explain the microbiological signals: all four BATCH-099 historian events and all 100 operator events are severity 'normal', and the only historian high-severity events (both PUMP-02 equipment_pressure_ratio 1.24 vs 1.1) belong to SYN-0015 and SYN-0090; DEV-0007 for SYN-0090 remains open with root cause not confirmed, and PUMP-02's only work order (WO-0010) closed one day before that excursion. The deviations source and source_review.pdf agree on all eight deviations; the package manifest declares the inventory and a synthetic-data notice but no quality-state notes. Missing evidence common to all candidate explanations: root-cause analyses for the open deviations, the site SOP for action-level escalation and disposition with open deviations, independent retests, environmental-control records for the process support area, and post-cutoff QA records; scanned-PDF values remain unverified OCR pending human visual review. The three-batch recurrence (2024-12, 2025-01, 2025-03) with rising magnitude, the same test and the same line supports a systemic upstream microbiological control hypothesis (H-01/H-02) over a batch-specific or analytical-error explanation, but no causal mechanism is confirmed in the scoped evidence.

The 'missing_source_time' flags on the checked clock_quality candidates are a clock/data-quality limitation of the analysis view, not a process excursion: the flagged source records carry explicit occurred_at/sample_collected_at values, the flagged members are in-limit constants (action_limit 1.0, alert_limit 0.7) and in-limit results with status normal/pass, and all checked records are synthetic_factory_signal rows (SYN- entities) rather than production batches.

microbiology_results mirrors lims_export for the action-level records: status='action' cells occur at identical source rows and entities (LAB-0010/SYN-0004, LAB-0225/BATCH-075, LAB-0255/BATCH-084, LAB-0300/BATCH-099) in both files, consistent with the lead's observation that the microbiology record for LAB-0300 mirrors LIMS LAB-0300.

Each of the BATCH-099 and BATCH-084 action records appears in both the local review and the scanned review with timezone-qualified release timestamps (local review: 2025-03-12T05:15:00-07:00 for LAB-0300 and 2025-01-04T05:25:00-07:00 for LAB-0255; scanned OCR lines: 2025-03-12T12:15:00Z and 2025-01-04T12:25:00Z). For BATCH-075 the scanned timestamp is OCR-corrupted and not comparable.

No process/equipment excursion is recorded for BATCH-099 in either the historian export or the PDF through 11:25:00Z; the action-level lab signals (LIMS bioburden certified by b099-bioburden-pct-of-action, EM certified by b099-em-vs-action) have no corresponding abnormal process event in these sources. Absence of a recorded excursion is not evidence the process stayed in control after 11:25:00Z.

The 11:25:00Z-12:15:00Z window is a coverage gap in the historian export and the PDF (both end at PROC-0400 for BATCH-099). This is a recording/export limitation, and no inference about process behavior in that window is possible from these sources.

The four clock_quality candidates are screening artifacts: the flagged series are limit-like columns (expected_high/expected_low/value) whose screening time windows are null, while every member cell carries a populated calendar timestamp, an in-range value and severity 'normal'. They do not indicate missing event timestamps or a process fault; the exact flag trigger (series time-window vs elapsed-clock basis) was not verified within budget.

WO-0010 (PUMP-02, closed 2025-01-29T21:00:00Z, linked to SYN-0090) preceding SYN-0090's 2025-01-30T10:00:00Z out-of-range event is a temporal association in the records only.
